title: What is ours
hook: our judgments, impulses, desires and aversions are ours; body, property, reputation and office are not (Enchiridion 1)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the enchiridion, the little book kept in the hand. Your line was keep it at hand. Is your note still in your pocket? Day three hundred thirty-three.

Page one of the handbook is not a pep talk. It's a sorting job. Two piles. Into the first goes everything that is really yours. Into the second, everything else. That's section one. No warm-up, no story, no promise. Epictetus seems to think that if this one sorting goes wrong, nothing else in the book will help, and if it goes right, the rest will start to make sense on its own. So before the handbook says anything about living well, it asks a plainer question. Today: what is ours.
screen: `PAGE ONE: A SORTING JOB.` → `TWO PILES.` → `WHAT IS OURS?`

segments.voice: First, the line itself. In George Long's translation of 1877, the handbook begins: "Of things some are in our power, and others are not." Then the lists. In our power: our opinions, our impulses toward things, our desires, our aversions. In a word, whatever is our own doing. Not in our power: the body, property, reputation, office. In a word, whatever is not our own doing. Second, the surprise. Look what's in the second pile. Your own body. Your good name. Your job. On a list of what's mine, those might come first. Epictetus says no: your body can get sick without asking you, your reputation lives in other people's heads, your job can be taken by a letter. What you do with all of it, how you judge it, what you reach for and what you push away, that stays with you. Third, why it matters. The things in our power, he says, are free by nature, nothing can block them. The things not in our power are weak, slavish, easily blocked, and belong to others. Treat the second pile as if it were the first, and you'll be frustrated, he warns, and you'll blame gods and people. Fourth, the tool. When something harsh shows up, he suggests saying to it: you are an appearance, not necessarily the thing you seem. Then ask one question. Is this in my power or not? If it isn't, be ready to say: it is nothing to me. That sounds cold at first. Epictetus means something narrower. Not that it doesn't matter, but that it isn't where your work is. Your work starts here.
screen: `SOME THINGS ARE IN OUR POWER.` · `BODY, PROPERTY, NAME: NOT OURS.` · `FREE BY NATURE, OR EASILY BLOCKED.` · `ASK: IS THIS IN MY POWER?` · then, large: `START HERE.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and paper, or do it in your head. Draw a line down the middle. On the left, list three things that are yours in Epictetus' sense: maybe how you'll speak to someone today, what you'll aim at, what you'll let go of. On the right, list three that aren't: the weather, a decision someone else is making, how a test comes back. Read both lists slowly. Then rest your eyes on the left side, and breathe. The bell holds the time.
George Long, whose 1877 translation opens the handbook's first sorting: our judgments, impulses, desires and aversions, not our body, property, reputation or office. Today's word.
Your line: start here. The first time today you feel stuck or stirred up, ask Epictetus' question: is this in my power? Then start there. Day three hundred thirty-three.

howItsDone: People who practice Stoicism often sort a worry into what is up to them and what isn't, sometimes on paper in two columns, and put their effort into the first.

myth: Epictetus puts your own body in the pile of things that are yours
the body is in the second pile: it can get sick without asking you.
the handbook opens with the line about what is and isn't in our power
it's section one, before anything else.
"it is nothing to me" means nothing outside you matters
it means that isn't where your own work lies.

fork.setup: your boss hasn't answered your email all day. what does Epictetus' first question ask you to do?
options: refresh the inbox until they answer.
ask: is this in my power or not?
fork.reveal: the handbook's first tool is the question: is this in my power? Their reply isn't. What you do next is.
